title: Catalpol alleviates heat stroke-induced liver injury in mice by downregulating the JAK/STAT signaling pathway.
authors: Ji, Xin Ye; Feng, Jian Ting; Zhou, Zong Yuan; Zhang, Yan Yuan; Ma, Shao Zhuang; Wang, Xiao Qin; Zhang, Bo
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究梓醇对热射病肝损伤的保护作用及JAK/STAT通路调控，仅含分子对接但无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Heat stroke (HS) generated liver injury is a lethal emergency that occurs when the body is exposed to temperatures up to 40  degrees C for a few hours. PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic prospects of Catalpol (CA) from the blood-cooling herb Rehamanniae Radix on liver injury by HS. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: A murine HS model (41 +/- 0.5  degrees C, 60 +/- 5 % relative humidity) and two cell lines (lipopolysaccharide + 42  degrees C) were used to assess the protective effects of CA on physiological, pathological, and biochemical features in silico, in vivo, and in vitro. RESULTS: CA treatment significantly improved survival rates in vivo and cell viability in vitro over those of the untreated group. Additionally, CA treatment reduced core body temperature, enhanced survival time, and mitigated liver tissue damage. Furthermore, CA treatment also reduced the activities of AST and ALT enzymes in the serum samples of HS mice. Molecular docking analysis of the 28 overlapping targets between HS and CA revealed that CA has strong binding affinities for the top 15 targets. These targets are primarily involved in nine major signaling pathways, with the JAK-STAT pathway being highly associated with the other eight pathways. Our findings also indicate that CA treatment significantly downregulated the expression of proinflammatory cytokines both in vivo and in vitro while upregulating the expression of anti-inflammatory cytokines. Moreover, CA treatment reduced the levels of JAK2, phospho-STAT5, and phospho-STAT3 both in vivo and in vitro, which is consistent with its inhibition of the apoptotic markers p53, Bcl2, and Bax. CONCLUSIONS: Heat stroke-induced liver injury was inhibited by CA through the downregulation of JAK/STAT signaling.
abstract_zh: 背景：热射病（HS）引起的肝损伤是一种致命性急症，当身体暴露于高达40摄氏度的温度数小时时发生。目的：本研究旨在评估来自凉血药材地黄的梓醇（Catalpol, CA）对热射病所致肝损伤的治疗前景。研究设计与方法：使用小鼠热射病模型（41 ± 0.5摄氏度，60 ± 5%相对湿度）和两种细胞系（脂多糖 + 42摄氏度），在计算机模拟、体内和体外评估CA对生理、病理和生化特征的保护作用。结果：与未治疗组相比，CA治疗显著提高了体内存活率和体外细胞活力。此外，CA治疗降低了核心体温，延长了存活时间，并减轻了肝组织损伤。进一步地，CA治疗还降低了热射病小鼠血清样本中AST和ALT酶的活性。对热射病和CA之间28个重叠靶点的分子对接分析显示，CA对前15个靶点具有强结合亲和力。这些靶点主要涉及九条主要信号通路，其中JAK-STAT通路与其他八条通路高度相关。我们的发现还表明，CA治疗在体内和体外均显著下调了促炎细胞因子的表达，同时上调了抗炎细胞因子的表达。此外，CA治疗在体内和体外均降低了JAK2、磷酸化STAT5和磷酸化STAT3的水平，这与其对凋亡标志物p53、Bcl2和Bax的抑制作用一致。结论：热射病诱导的肝损伤通过下调JAK/STAT信号通路被CA抑制。
